title: Titanium AUV Propeller Shaft
alloyReason: Ti-6Al-4V ELI (Grade 23, UNS R56401) is mandated for this deep sea application where ELI elements (O <=0.13%, Fe <=0.25%) provide superior fracture toughness (KIC >100 MPa-m0.5) and fatigue resistance vs standard Grade 5. This rationale is driven by autonomous underwater vehicle propeller shaft and specific design requirements.
process: Ring forging radial-axial for deep sea geometry
CNC turn-bore operation with 0.5mm corner radius
TIG welding autogenous with 0.5mm corner radius
Hydrostatic pressure test with 0.5mm corner radius
surfaceTreatment: Heavy-duty passivation 25% HNO3 45min per ASTM B600 for maximum chloride pitting resistance in seawater — tailored for autonomous underwater vehicle application
commonFailures: Crevice corrosion under biofouling in stagnant seawater - mitigated by CP-Ti Grade 2 + ICCP system — critical for autonomous underwater vehicle performance

faq.q: What specific material properties make Titanium AUV Propeller Shaft suitable for Autonomous underwater vehicle propeller shaft?
faq.a: Titanium AUV Propeller Shaft uses Grade 5 Ti-6Al-4V because its yield strength, fatigue endurance, and corrosion resistance directly address deep sea operational demands. The alloy's specific strength enables mass reduction without section compromise, while the TiO2 passivation ensures long-term environmental resistance.

faq.q: What are the critical dimensional tolerances for Titanium AUV Propeller Shaft?
faq.a: Standard machining tolerance for Titanium AUV Propeller Shaft is +/-0.05mm (ISO 2768-m). Functional mating surfaces are held to +/-0.025mm with Ra 0.8um finish, verified specifically for autonomous underwater vehicle requirements. Threaded features conform to ISO 965-2 Class 6g, verified with calibrated Go/No-Go ring gauges on 100% of production.

faq.q: Does Titanium AUV Propeller Shaft require any post-machining surface treatment?
faq.a: Yes. autonomous underwater vehicle components require Heavy-duty passivation 25% HNO3 45min per ASTM B600 for maximum chloride pitting resistance in seawater — tailored for autonomous underwater vehicle application. This restores the natural TiO2 passive layer removed during machining and provides the required surface properties for the specific service environment. Key parameters include surface finish Ra 0.8um and passive layer thickness verification per applicable standards.

faq.q: What quality documentation is included with Titanium AUV Propeller Shaft shipments?
faq.a: Each shipment of Titanium AUV Propeller Shaft includes: (1) EN 10204 Type 3.1 MTR with full chemical analysis and mechanical properties; (2) Certificate of Conformance confirming all processes meet autonomous underwater vehicle specifications; (3) Dimensional inspection report with actual vs nominal measurements on critical features; (4) Surface roughness certification per applicable standards. FAIR available on request.

faq.q: What is the MOQ and typical lead time for AUV shaft / Underwater shaft deep sea components?
faq.a: Standard MOQ: 1 unit for prototype evaluation. Production lead time: 15-25 business days depending on quantity. Rush orders (3-5 days) available. Contact our supply chain team for volume-based tiered pricing.
